findings.evidence: The candidate edits the freshness-check paragraph (diff line 49) to say omitting `--tier` confirms the authored tier. It leaves the next sentence unchanged: "Passing `--profile` explicitly still works exactly as before (useful for a legacy package with no receipt, or for a deliberate override)". `_RemovedProfile` makes `route-claude --profile` and `route-codex --profile` exit with a parser error. The spec requirement says "`--profile` SHALL be refused ... Source docs and hints SHALL name only R1/R2/R3 for these commands."
findings.summary: docs/engineering/model-routing.md still tells readers that `--profile` works on the route commands. The new requirement says `--profile` is refused and that source docs name only R1/R2/R3 for these commands.

findings.evidence: The text after the codex example (diff line 62) reads "`routine` and `standard` (... passed explicitly) immediately launch ... while `complex` (derived from `R3`, or passed explicitly) records the route". The claude paragraph (diff line 71) reads "`complex` (derived from `R3`, or passed explicitly)". Both are about the route commands, which now take only tiers.
findings.summary: The model-routing.md prose around the route commands still uses the profile names routine/standard/complex as if they were the operator-facing vocabulary. This leaves the dual naming the change was meant to remove.
